// What to look for: this shader is INVALID -- an amplification-shader payload may not
// contain a resource -- so the expected result is a clean error diagnostic.
//
// Instead both DXC panes die inside the compiler. Check the compiler's exit status,
// not the (empty) output: on Windows this is an access violation reading address 0
// (0xC0000005); on Compiler Explorer's Linux builds it is a segmentation fault. Either
// way no diagnostic is produced and no DXIL is emitted.
//
// dxc 1.6.2112 is the oldest DXC on Compiler Explorer. Locally, every release from
// v1.5.2010 (the first shipping as_6_5) through v1.9.2607 fails the same way, so the
// window CE can show is the tail of a history that has never been clean.
//
// Compiler Explorer builds are Release builds. The assert that names the issue --
// DXASSERT_NOMSG(Ty) in hlsl::dxilutil::WrapInArrayTypes, called from
// TranslatePtrIfUsedByLoweredFn -- is compiled out here, so CE cannot show it. What CE
// does show is that removing the assert does not remove the bug: the same null type
// reaches the allocation and faults. CE corroborates the local Debug build; it does not
// overrule it.
//
// Control: change "Texture2D<float4> texture;" to "uint value;" and it compiles cleanly.
